title: Transferable KV Fingerprint and Proactive Slot-Scarcity Mitigation for Paged Attention
creator: Priya Raman
description: Goal: Reduce prefill latency spikes and fragment churn on multi-tenant paged KV by introducing compact transferable fingerprints for resident KV slots plus a proactive slot-scarcity mitigation strategy. Scope: allocation fingerprinting, slot transfer protocol, scarcity detector (moving-watermark + short-term demand forecasting), compact-on-read eviction glue, and a probe-driven prefill hedging path. Acceptance criteria: 1) 25-40% reduction in prefill tail latency (p95-p99) for synthetic mixed-length workloads; 2) measurable decrease in high-frequency fragment churn (>10% drop in touch turnover rate) across 500-host experiments; 3) no regression in single-request median latency; 4) safe fallbacks to existing eviction when transfer cannot be completed within lease window.
implementation_notes: Design introduces a 32-bit transferable fingerprint attached to each slot reservation that represents a compacted recent-touch signature plus tenant affinity tag. On slot handoff, the runtime attempts a fast ephemeral transfer (intra-shard fast-path) where the receiving decoder can reuse KV pages without full restore. If transfer fails (timeout or checksum mismatch), we fall back to standard cold-restore + compact-on-read where reads trigger opportunistic defragging of small adjacent fragments. Scarcity detector will compute per-shard reservoir pressure using EWMA of slot requests and prefill attempt rate; when above threshold, new requests are steered to compatible kernel variants with lighter memory footprint. Kernel routing changes require adding a handshake to the kernel scheduler API to accept a transfer token. All changes feature feature-flag gating and metrics instrumentation for rollout.
design_decisions: 1) Use a fixed-width (32-bit) fingerprint instead of variable bloom to minimize RPC/slot metadata overhead; collision risk mitigated by short lease windows and idempotent transfer semantics. 2) Prefer transfer-on-prefill (prefill-as-opportunistic-handoff) vs deferring to eviction, to increase reuse of warm fragments for bursty tenants. 3) Scarcity detector threshold uses relative reservoir pressure to avoid global threshold tuning per-hardware. 4) Compact-on-read chosen over eager compaction to avoid extra CPU cycles during steady-state serving.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fingerprint collisions could cause incorrect reuse leading to corrupted decoder state. Mitigation: Add checksum validation and conservative mismatch fallback that triggers full restore. Risk: Transfer protocol adds latency to prefill path. Mitigation: Make transfer opportunistic and abortable; measure added median latency in synthetic bench. Risk: Multi-tenant fairness under scarcity. Mitigation: implement per-tenant weighted soft-quotas and admission backoff with token-bucket shaping.
comments: 2026-01-14: Kickoff meeting with serving runtime and kernel teams. Agreed on 32-bit fingerprint and transfer handshake. Action: Evan to prototype transfer token format.
2026-01-28: Prototype shows transfer succeed rate ~78% on local mix workloads; observed 6% median latency increase on prefill path without optimizations. Need microbench kernel handshake path.
2026-02-05: Design review with PM and Security. PM requested tenant-weighted quotas; security requested checksum validation and audit events for transfers. Added audit events to spec.
2026-02-18: Implemented scarcity detector EWMA in runtime; initial threshold causing ~12% of requests to be steered — tuned down after ablation tests. Linked PR 1892 opened.

2026-02-25: Performance run on 200-host cluster: p95 prefill latency reduced 28% for mixed-length traffic when transfer succeeds; fragment touch turnover down ~14%. Still failing ~8% transfers due to cold-shard races; tracking as follow-up.
2026-03-02: Merged compact-on-read helper and added metrics for transfer success/fallback. Next: implement kernel handshake in kernel-scheduler PR 1918 and add e2e canary with feature flag.
2026-03-05: Design feedback from infra: add observability for per-tenant handoff counts and a debug dump for mismatched fingerprints. Evan to add in follow-up PR.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint generation/verification, integration tests for intra-shard transfer (simulated latency and checksum error injections), and stress-run on 500-host cluster with synthetic workloads: short-sequence heavy burst, long-sequence steady, and mixed. Canary rollout: 5% traffic in staging, 10% in prod small shard groups, monitor p99/p95, transfer-fail-rate, fragment-reuse-rate, and eviction churn. If transfer-fail-rate > 15% or p99 increases > 10%, automatic rollback via feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: p95 prefill latency reduction between 25% and 40% on mixed workloads
fragment touch turnover rate reduced by at least 10% in cluster runs
transfer fallback path is exercised < 15% of attempts after tuning
end-to-end canary does not increase error rate or violate latency SLOs
